decisions.statement: A copy is judged on where the copy puts things.
A move is judged on where the move puts things.
A tool told to write the file the tool reads is judged on every path the tool names.
The flag saying so is what parts that tool from the same tool reading.
A descriptor redirected onto another descriptor is no path.
A descriptor redirected onto another descriptor is passed over.
A redirect reading in names what a call is handed rather than where the call lands.
A command that makes or takes away a file is judged on every path the command names.
A prefix that only runs the call behind the prefix does not hide the call from this hook.
A program's own text is not read.
A redirect is read outside the body a heredoc carries rather than inside that body.
A body handed to a program is read for the paths that body names.
A call a heredoc body carries is data rather than a call.
A read through a program is not parted from a write through the program.
An interpreter is judged on every path the call handing that interpreter a program names.
A removal naming a symlink itself is judged where the link is rather than where the link points.
A link made over a symlink itself and told not to follow it is judged where the link is.
A link made over a symlink without that flag is judged where the link points.
A path naming a symlink itself ends in the symlink's own name.
A path opening with a tilde names the home directory rather than a folder here.
A tilde the shell would leave alone for being quoted names a folder here.
A landing the repository ignores is not guarded.
A landing inside the index is judged where the path points.
A landing elsewhere under the folder git does not track is answered with the sweep.
That landing is guarded even where the repository ignores it.
No refusal over that folder names a change.
A landing inside the index is guarded even where the repository ignores that landing.
The repository's ignore rules are read only over a landing that would otherwise be refused.
The ways a shell writes a file are sampled here rather than named in full.
No shell write reaches inside a guarded root.
A call another program builds is judged as a call written on the line is.
A payload this cannot read judges nothing and exits so the dispatch refuses.
A payload that parses and is not an object is a payload this cannot read.
A path a word represents rather than spells is judged as a spelled path is.

definition: the hook refusing a shell write that lands inside akasha
